decisions.decision: T-3-08 threat-model mitigation amended 2026-07-26 (attempt #2, actual root cause): added CLOUDSDK_PYTHON_SITEPACKAGES=1 env var + check_hashes=if_fast_else_skip boto config fallback + a gsutil version -l pre-flight verification cell
decisions.rationale: Confirmed via GoogleCloudPlatform/gsutil GitHub issue #1429: gsutil (part of Google Cloud SDK) runs its own bundled, isolated Python interpreter, completely separate from the Colab kernel's Python. The earlier crcmod reinstall (260726-gj6) succeeded in the KERNEL's Python but was invisible to gsutil's bundled interpreter, so the CRC32C hash computation stayed on the slow pure-Python path regardless of destination — explaining why moving off Drive didn't help. CLOUDSDK_PYTHON_SITEPACKAGES=1 makes gsutil's bundled interpreter fall back to the kernel's site-packages where crcmod's C extension actually landed. As a safety net (the GitHub issue notes this fallback can fail on Python ABI mismatches), check_hashes=if_fast_else_skip (gsutil's own officially-sanctioned partial integrity-check skip, only triggers when the C extension is genuinely unavailable) was also configured via a /content/.boto file. A pre-flight cell running gsutil version -l lets the user confirm success BEFORE attempting the full 11.6GB download again, to avoid a fourth blind-retry cycle.

Discovered mid-session: this repo's LIBERO/ is its own nested git repo, entirely gitignored by the main repo, but on case-insensitive macOS a pre-existing (Phase 1) convention has files landing under a lowercase 'libero/' path tracked by the MAIN repo's git (not LIBERO's own git) — this is accepted/pre-existing, not something to 'fix' mid-phase. Also discovered: Colab kernels cache Python module imports across cell re-runs — re-syncing a fixed source file via the unzip cell does NOT reload already-imported modules; a genuine Runtime > Restart session is required, not just re-running cells. This caused one confusing false-repeat-error round-trip during debugging; flagged as advisory for any future Colab debugging in this project. Lesson from 260726-epz: openpi tracks main with no pinned release — its LIBERO config names (pi0_fast_libero/pi0_libero) were deprecated in favor of pi05_libero between plan-time and first live run; re-verify openpi's serve_policy.py/README/config.py directly against source before trusting any previously-researched config name if this project's openpi checkout advances again. Lesson from 260726-gj6+260726-hbb (important — a misdiagnosis happened here): an identical gsutil failure ('N files/objects could not be transferred' after crcmod C-extension warnings) persisted across two different download destinations (Drive-mounted, then local disk), which falsified the first root-cause theory (Drive FUSE unreliability). The ACTUAL cause was that gsutil (Google Cloud SDK) uses its own bundled, isolated Python interpreter that never sees packages pip-installed into the Colab kernel — so 'pip install crcmod' in a notebook cell does NOT make gsutil see the compiled extension, regardless of where the download is going. The general lesson: when a fix doesn't change an error's exact wording/behavior at all after a live re-test, suspect the fix targeted a coincidental/secondary factor, not the actual mechanism — re-derive from the raw traceback and the specific tool's own architecture (here, gsutil's bundled-interpreter isolation is a well-known, documented gsutil/Cloud-SDK quirk, findable by searching the tool's own GitHub issues) rather than patching the most visible symptom (the destination path, which was mentioned in the error text) a second time.
